updateNote: DRAFT for counsel review — not active in the product. Encoded from Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR). Review each control against the Regulation, EDPB guidelines and current enforcement practice; note corrections in the study Excel; the reviewed version becomes v1.0.0 on your sign-off.

controls.title: Lawful basis identified for every processing activity
controls.description: Each processing purpose is mapped to one of the six lawful bases (consent, contract, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, legitimate interests) and the mapping is documented.
controls.evidenceRequired: Processing register or data map showing purpose → lawful basis per activity.
controls.remediation: Inventory all processing activities and assign a lawful basis to each; where none fits, stop the processing.

controls.title: Legitimate-interests assessments (LIA) on file
controls.description: Where legitimate interests is the basis, a balancing test (LIA) exists weighing the controller's interest against the data subject's rights.
controls.evidenceRequired: LIA document per legitimate-interests processing activity.
controls.remediation: Run and record a three-part LIA (purpose, necessity, balancing) for each such activity.

controls.title: Purpose limitation respected
controls.description: Personal data collected for specified purposes is not further processed incompatibly with those purposes.
controls.evidenceRequired: Purpose register; change-control for new uses of existing data.
controls.remediation: Gate any new use of held data through a compatibility assessment.

controls.title: Data minimisation practised
controls.description: Only data adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary is collected and retained.
controls.evidenceRequired: Field-level review of forms and databases against purposes.
controls.remediation: Remove fields and stores not justified by a documented purpose.

controls.title: Special-category data handled under Art. 9 condition
controls.description: Processing of special categories (health, biometrics, beliefs, etc.) relies on an explicit Art. 9(2) condition in addition to the Art. 6 basis.
controls.evidenceRequired: Register entry naming the Art. 9(2) condition per special-category activity.
controls.remediation: Identify special-category flows; document the condition or cease processing.

controls.title: Children's data: age verification and parental consent
controls.description: Information-society services offered to children obtain parental consent below the applicable member-state age (13–16).
controls.evidenceRequired: Age-gate design; consent flow for minors; member-state age matrix if multi-country.
controls.remediation: Implement age verification and verifiable parental consent.

controls.title: Consent is freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous
controls.description: Where consent is the basis: no pre-ticked boxes, no bundling with terms, granular per purpose, affirmative act required.
controls.evidenceRequired: Consent UI screenshots per collection point; consent text.
controls.remediation: Redesign consent capture to granular, unbundled, opt-in interactions.

controls.title: Consent records demonstrate who, when, what, how
controls.description: The controller can demonstrate that consent was given: timestamped records tying subject, purpose, text version and capture mechanism.
controls.evidenceRequired: Consent log excerpt (masked) showing the four elements.
controls.remediation: Implement consent receipts / logging keyed to the consent-text version.

controls.title: Withdrawal as easy as giving consent
controls.description: Subjects can withdraw consent at any time, as easily as they gave it, and are told so before consenting.
controls.evidenceRequired: Withdrawal mechanism (UI/link); propagation to downstream processing.
controls.remediation: Add one-step withdrawal; wire it to stop dependent processing.

controls.title: Privacy notice contains all Art. 13/14 elements
controls.description: Notices identify the controller, DPO contact, purposes and bases, recipients, transfers and safeguards, retention, all subject rights, complaint right, and automated decision-making logic.
controls.evidenceRequired: Published notice mapped element-by-element to Art. 13/14.
controls.remediation: Gap-map the notice against Art. 13/14 and republish.

controls.title: Notice provided at collection (or within one month if indirect)
controls.description: Information is given when data is obtained from the subject; for indirect collection, within a month or at first contact.
controls.evidenceRequired: Collection-point inventory showing notice delivery; process for indirect sources.
controls.remediation: Attach notice links to every form and third-party intake.

controls.title: Notices are concise, intelligible, accessible
controls.description: Plain language, layered where useful, available in the languages of the audience served.
controls.evidenceRequired: Readability review; language coverage vs customer base.
controls.remediation: Rewrite in plain language; add layers/translations.

controls.title: Access requests fulfilled within one month
controls.description: A workflow receives, verifies identity for, and fulfils subject-access requests within one month (extendable by two with notice).
controls.evidenceRequired: DSAR procedure; request log with dates showing SLA adherence.
controls.remediation: Stand up a DSAR intake with identity verification and deadline tracking.

controls.title: Rectification and erasure operational
controls.description: Correction and deletion (where a ground applies) execute across all systems, including backups policy and onward notification to recipients.
controls.evidenceRequired: Erasure runbook covering every data store; recipient-notification step.
controls.remediation: Map data stores; script erasure; add Art. 19 recipient notification.

controls.title: Restriction and objection honoured
controls.description: Processing can be flagged restricted; objections (incl. to direct marketing — absolute) stop the processing.
controls.evidenceRequired: Restriction flag in systems; marketing-suppression list.
controls.remediation: Add restriction states and an always-honoured marketing opt-out.

controls.title: Portability delivered in machine-readable form
controls.description: For consent/contract-based automated processing, subjects can receive their data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
controls.evidenceRequired: Export capability demonstration (e.g. JSON/CSV bundle).
controls.remediation: Build a per-subject structured export.

controls.title: Automated decisions: safeguards and human review
controls.description: Solely automated decisions with legal/significant effects occur only under Art. 22(2) exceptions, with human-intervention rights.
controls.evidenceRequired: Inventory of automated decisioning; safeguard description.
controls.remediation: Add human review path or remove sole-automation for significant decisions.

controls.title: Accountability: policies and evidence of compliance
controls.description: The controller can demonstrate compliance: data-protection policy set, responsibilities assigned, reviews scheduled.
controls.evidenceRequired: Policy suite; review calendar; management sign-off.
controls.remediation: Adopt and evidence a data-protection programme.

controls.title: DPO appointed where required (and registered)
controls.description: Where core activities involve large-scale monitoring or special categories, a DPO is designated, resourced, independent, and notified to the authority.
controls.evidenceRequired: DPO designation; authority notification; reporting line.
controls.remediation: Assess the Art. 37 trigger; appoint and register a DPO if met.

controls.title: EU representative appointed if controller is outside the EU
controls.description: Non-EU controllers/processors targeting EU subjects have designated a representative in a relevant member state.
controls.evidenceRequired: Representative appointment letter; contact published in notices.
controls.remediation: Appoint an Art. 27 representative and name them in the notice.

controls.title: Staff training and confidentiality commitments
controls.description: Persons acting under authority process only on instructions and are trained; confidentiality undertakings are in place.
controls.evidenceRequired: Training records; confidentiality clauses.
controls.remediation: Run annual privacy training; add confidentiality terms to contracts.

controls.title: Records of processing activities maintained
controls.description: A current Art. 30 register exists (purposes, categories, recipients, transfers, retention, security measures) for controller and processor roles.
controls.evidenceRequired: The register itself, with a last-reviewed date.
controls.remediation: Build the Art. 30 register; assign an owner; review quarterly.

controls.title: DPIAs performed for high-risk processing
controls.description: A screening process identifies high-risk processing (systematic monitoring, large-scale special categories, etc.) and full DPIAs are performed before starting.
controls.evidenceRequired: DPIA screening criteria; completed DPIAs for qualifying activities.
controls.remediation: Adopt DPIA screening in project intake; complete DPIAs for live high-risk processing.

controls.title: Prior consultation where residual risk stays high
controls.description: Where a DPIA leaves high residual risk unmitigated, the supervisory authority is consulted before processing.
controls.evidenceRequired: Consultation record or documented determination that none was required.
controls.remediation: Add a prior-consultation gate to the DPIA process.

controls.title: Data protection by design in change management
controls.description: Privacy requirements (minimisation, pseudonymisation, purpose binding) are considered at design time for new systems and features.
controls.evidenceRequired: Design-review checklist including privacy; example from a recent project.
controls.remediation: Add privacy criteria to the definition-of-done for new work.

controls.title: Privacy-protective defaults
controls.description: By default, only necessary data is processed; visibility and sharing default to the most private setting.
controls.evidenceRequired: Default-settings review of user-facing products.
controls.remediation: Flip defaults to opt-in for any non-essential processing.

controls.title: Technical and organisational measures appropriate to risk
controls.description: Security measures (encryption, access control, resilience, testing) are chosen from a documented risk assessment.
controls.evidenceRequired: Security risk assessment; measures mapped to risks.
controls.remediation: Run a risk assessment; document the measure-to-risk mapping.

controls.title: Encryption and pseudonymisation applied where appropriate
controls.description: Personal data is encrypted in transit and at rest where appropriate; pseudonymisation reduces identifiability in analytics/testing.
controls.evidenceRequired: Encryption inventory (TLS, at-rest); pseudonymisation practice for secondary uses.
controls.remediation: Close encryption gaps; pseudonymise non-production data.

controls.title: Access on need-to-know with joiner/mover/leaver control
controls.description: Role-based access, timely revocation, and periodic access reviews cover employees and outsourced staff.
controls.evidenceRequired: Access matrix; last access-review record; leaver checklist.
controls.remediation: Implement RBAC with quarterly reviews and same-day revocation.

controls.title: Regular testing of security effectiveness
controls.description: A process regularly tests and evaluates measures (pen tests, restore drills, control audits).
controls.evidenceRequired: Latest test reports and remediation tracking.
controls.remediation: Schedule annual penetration testing and recovery drills.

controls.title: Breach notification to authority within 72 hours
controls.description: A rehearsed process detects, assesses and notifies the supervisory authority within 72 hours unless risk is unlikely, with documented reasoning either way.
controls.evidenceRequired: Incident-response plan; breach register incl. no-notify rationales; drill record.
controls.remediation: Adopt a 72-hour runbook; keep an Art. 33(5) breach register; rehearse annually.

controls.title: High-risk breaches communicated to data subjects
controls.description: Where a breach likely poses high risk to individuals, they are informed without undue delay in clear language.
controls.evidenceRequired: Subject-communication templates; criteria for the high-risk call.
controls.remediation: Prepare Art. 34 communication templates and decision criteria.

controls.title: Art. 28 contracts with every processor
controls.description: Every processor is bound by a contract containing the mandatory clauses (instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processors, assistance, deletion/return, audit).
controls.evidenceRequired: Processor inventory with DPA status per vendor.
controls.remediation: Inventory processors; execute DPAs; remediate or replace non-signers.

controls.title: Sub-processor authorisation and flow-down
controls.description: Sub-processors are engaged only with authorisation and under equivalent obligations.
controls.evidenceRequired: Sub-processor lists from key vendors; authorisation mechanism.
controls.remediation: Require sub-processor disclosure and approval rights in DPAs.

controls.title: Joint-controller arrangements documented
controls.description: Where purposes/means are jointly determined, an arrangement allocates responsibilities and its essence is available to subjects.
controls.evidenceRequired: Joint-controller agreement(s); notice text reflecting them.
controls.remediation: Identify joint arrangements; paper them under Art. 26.

controls.title: Transfer mechanism for every third-country transfer
controls.description: Each transfer outside the EEA rests on adequacy, appropriate safeguards (e.g. SCCs with transfer impact assessment), or a narrow derogation.
controls.evidenceRequired: Transfer register: destination, mechanism, TIA where SCCs used.
controls.remediation: Build the transfer register; execute SCCs + TIAs where needed.

controls.title: Transfer impact assessments after Schrems II
controls.description: SCC-based transfers are assessed for destination-country law and supplementary measures where surveillance risk exists.
controls.evidenceRequired: TIA per SCC transfer; supplementary measures adopted.
controls.remediation: Run TIAs on existing SCC transfers; add technical measures (encryption with EU-held keys) where indicated.

controls.title: Cookie consent before non-essential cookies
controls.description: Non-essential cookies/trackers fire only after valid consent; reject is as easy as accept.
controls.evidenceRequired: Scan showing no pre-consent tracker fires; banner with equal accept/reject.
controls.remediation: Deploy a CMP in prior-blocking mode with equal-prominence choices.

controls.title: Cookie inventory and policy published
controls.description: A current cookie table (name, purpose, duration, provider) is published and matches reality.
controls.evidenceRequired: Cookie policy page vs scan results.
controls.remediation: Generate the inventory from a scan and keep it synced.

controls.title: Transport security on all data-collection surfaces
controls.description: HTTPS everywhere with sound TLS configuration on every page collecting personal data.
controls.evidenceRequired: TLS scan of collection endpoints.
controls.remediation: Enforce HTTPS + HSTS; retire weak ciphers.

controls.title: Baseline security headers present
controls.description: CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protections and referrer policy reduce client-side data-leak risk.
controls.evidenceRequired: Header scan of primary domains.
controls.remediation: Add the baseline header set at the edge.
